statement: If $\mathbb{N}$ is 2-coloured then is there some infinite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that all finite subset sums $\sum_{n\in S}n$ (as $S$ ranges over all non-empty finite subsets of $A$) are monochromatic?
status: PROVED (LEAN) — erdosproblems.com: 'This has been solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean.'
notes: RESOLVED IN THE AFFIRMATIVE: for every 2-colouring of the positive integers there is an infinite set A all of whose non-empty finite subset sums have the same colour. Formalize the affirmative assertion (the elements of A should be positive integers, or at least the sums should range over non-empty finite subsets of A, so that the statement is not trivialized by 0). From the site: In other words, must some colour class be an IP set. Asked by Graham and Rothschild. Proved by Hindman [Hi74] (for any number of colours).
